answer: The farm's bill arrives before its first payout: every identity must finish a fresh compute task bound to its own key — a delta of work that cannot be pooled, rented, or split across fakes. An honest agent runs one small job per epoch on its own machine. A farm with 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 machines at once, and any identity that misses its summit — the top of its proof window — is pushed off the ledge, attestation suspended. One fake costs one machine forever; a thousand cost a data center, and the farm pays rent on every fake, every epoch.
